lessons.title: Telling the Time

items.exampleMeaning: It is a quarter past two.

lessons.tip: In German, we say 'Es ist...' to tell the time. Use 'nach' for past and 'halb' for half past.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Und wie spät ist es am Nachmittag?
dialogue.meaning: And what time is it in the afternoon?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: It is a quarter past two.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Guten Abend! Es ist halb vier.
dialogue.meaning: Good evening! It is half past three.

scenario.partnerRole: A local who can help with directions.
scenario.learnerRole: You are asking for the time and greeting the local.
scenario.brief: Ask the local what time it is and greet them. Use the phrases you learned about telling the time.
scenario.goal: You need to know the time.

lessons.title: Buying Tickets

items.example: Ich möchte ein Ticket nach Berlin.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a ticket to Berlin.

items.meaning: How much does the ticket cost?
items.example: Wie viel kostet das Ticket nach München?
items.exampleMeaning: How much does the ticket to Munich cost?

items.text: Ich möchte ein Ticket für den Zug.
items.meaning: I would like a ticket for the train.
items.example: Ich möchte ein Ticket für den Zug nach Frankfurt.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a ticket for the train to Frankfurt.
Do you have a fare ticket?

lessons.tip: When buying a ticket, use 'Ein Ticket, bitte.' to make a polite request. Asking about prices is important.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Wie viel kostet das Ticket nach Berlin?
dialogue.meaning: How much does the ticket to Berlin cost?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ich möchte ein Ticket für den Zug.
dialogue.meaning: I would like a ticket for the train.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, für Studenten gibt es Ermäßigungen.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, there are discounts for students.

scenario.partnerRole: A ticket seller at a train station.
scenario.brief: Ask the ticket seller for a ticket and inquire about the price and discounts.
scenario.goal: You need to buy a ticket.

lessons.title: Using the Present Tense
lessons.tip: In German, the verb changes based on the subject. 'Ich' means 'I', 'Du' means 'you (informal)', 'Er' means 'he', 'Wir' means 'we', and 'Sie' means 'they'.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: We are going to the cinema.

scenario.partnerRole: A friend who is curious about your travel plans.
scenario.learnerRole: You are explaining your travel plans.
scenario.brief: Tell your friend where you are going and how you will get there.
scenario.goal: You need to explain your travel plans.

lessons.title: Combining Everything

items.exampleMeaning: When are you going to Berlin?

items.example: Ich komme um fünf Uhr an.
Das ist toll, dass du fährst!
items.exampleMeaning: That is great that you are going!

items.example: Ich habe ein Ticket nach München.
items.exampleMeaning: I have a ticket to Munich.

lessons.tip: Asking 'Wann?' means you want to know the time of an event. Use 'Ich habe ein Ticket.' to confirm that you have a ticket.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: When are you going to Munich?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ich komme um fünf Uhr an.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, ich habe ein Ticket nach München.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I have a ticket to Munich.

scenario.partnerRole: A friend who is planning a trip.
scenario.learnerRole: You are discussing your travel plans.
scenario.brief: Share your travel details with your friend, including the time and your ticket status.
scenario.goal: You need to share your travel plans.
